## How the guide defines it

Not addressed in guide.

## How the guide uses it

Present on 245 pages and treated as the single largest swing factor in the book. p. 45 is a standalone feature, 'The Year of the Quarterback'. Every team page discusses the position, the win-total feature rests 22 of its 29 bets on it, and the Heisman material on p. 39 is explicitly framed as a quarterback market. Makinen's transition systems treat 'breaking in a new quarterback' as a mechanical trigger rather than a narrative flourish.

## Working definition — TTW DERIVED

The quality, experience and continuity of a team's starting quarterback, treated as an input to a projection rather than as a scouting judgement.

## Why it matters — TTW DERIVED

The guide's contributors reach for it first and most often. Where a returning starter and a returning coordinator coincide, the guide is bullish; where a new quarterback meets a new system, its decline systems fire.

## How bettors use it in this guide

Two distinct ways, and the guide keeps them apart: a *named* quarterback carrying a case (Arch Manning, LaNorris Sellers, Conner Weigman), versus 'a new quarterback' as a binary trigger inside a transition system, which is how Connecticut, Ohio, San Jose State and South Florida are handled.

## Where it appears

p. 45 for the feature; p. 39 for the Heisman framing; pp. 22–27 for the position as a win-total driver.
